snapped_doors_investigation_2026_08_17.rule: a red test we understand is worth more than a green one we have adjusted to (Rahul, 17 Aug). Do not touch the golden until the strip geometry is understood.
snapped_doors_investigation_2026_08_17.resolution: `DOOR_MIN_FT` was serving FIVE purposes and the `- 0.3` slack existed only to reconcile the strip-span floor with a real leaf width. Split into DOOR_LEAF_MIN/MAX_FT (a real door), DRAWN_GAP_MIN/MAX_FT (the opening in the linework), and NO floor at all on the strip span - measured: a strip is a property of the ROI close, not a doorway (doors that snap correctly show 0.00-0.18 ft of opening yet produce 2.24-3.05 ft strips).

SIMULATED_CORRECTION.method: rescale every measured room area by (8.80/ppf)^2 and re-run room_dims.match_pct. CAVEAT: computed from the room's BBOX, not its polygon, so absolute values differ from the live R-2 (this method reads 68.6 where the parser reads 60.7). Directional, not exact.
SIMULATED_CORRECTION.note: WORST gets WORSE (57.7 -> 33.7) because `dining` goes from slightly over to 33% over. A large net win that costs the worst room - report both, per the quartet rule.

scale_error_REMEASURED_ON_THE_SPLIT_SHEE.PROPOSAL: derive ppf from the R-2 matched pairs themselves - the median measured/printed SIDE ratio over all matched rooms (14 side samples on 7 rooms) - instead of `_room_dim_scale`'s 2-vote room-extent voting. Per §0.1 the printed dimensions outrank the column-box guess, and this uses 7x more of them.
scale_error_REMEASURED_ON_THE_SPLIT_SHEE.THE_OBJECTION_I_MUST_RAISE_AGAINST_MY_OW: IT IS CIRCULAR IN EXACTLY THE WAY THE p90 WAS. If ppf is fitted so the median measured/printed ratio is 1.0, then R-2's MEDIAN becomes ~100 BY CONSTRUCTION and can no longer judge the scale. What survives as a real measurement is R-2's SCATTER - `rooms_off` and `worst_match_pct` - which is not fitted. Any such change must be judged by an INDEPENDENT instrument.
scale_error_REMEASURED_ON_THE_SPLIT_SHEE.THE_INDEPENDENT_JUDGE: the §10.2 DIMENSION-ANCHOR instrument: it compares printed dimension VALUES against distances between detected wall faces, using the `dim` text route, and does NOT read room labels. GHATIKIA reads 29/52 endpoints = 56% today. If 7.19 is the right scale, that number must RISE; if it does not, the scale change is not supported by anything independent and must not ship. THAT is the acceptance test, not R-2's median.

seal_split_NOT_SEPARABLE_AT_THIS_LAYER_2.judged_footprint_first_and_it_stopped_th: the ordering Rahul set - footprint before any room number - ended the experiment in one run. No room, carpet or R-2 figure was read, because none of them would have meant anything under a footprint down 17-58%.
seal_split_NOT_SEPARABLE_AT_THIS_LAYER_2.THE_PLAIN_ANSWER: THE TWO JOBS ARE NOT SEPARABLE AT THIS LAYER. `_footprint_from_walls` is not an independent envelope-closer; it is a REFINEMENT ON TOP OF THE SEAL. `_free_ring_endpoints` looks for gap endpoints in a mask whose DOORWAYS ARE ALREADY CLOSED - on the raw mask every doorway is itself a ring gap, the relative bound rejects them, and the ring never closes. The seal is what makes the ring's input ring-shaped.
seal_split_NOT_SEPARABLE_AT_THIS_LAYER_2.so_the_dependency_runs_both_ways: the ring is downstream of the seal (23 Aug finding) AND the ring cannot function without it (this finding). They are one operation in two pieces, not two operations sharing a constant.
seal_split_NOT_SEPARABLE_AT_THIS_LAYER_2.what_a_real_split_would_need: an envelope closer that does not presuppose a closed-doorway mask - i.e. one that works from the drawn wall SEGMENTS rather than from a raster whose gaps it cannot tell apart. `_free_ring_endpoints` already takes `seg_px`; a version that bridges between SEGMENT ends only, ignoring raster gaps entirely, would be independent of the seal. NOT PROPOSED, NOT BUILT - recorded as the only remaining direction.
